chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him about a man who pronounced zihar against his wife five times or more. He said: Upon him, for each time, is an expiation.

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Zihar, a pre-Islamic and early Islamic form of divorce where a husband compares his wife to his mother's back, requiring expiation.
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation or atonement, a ritual act or payment required to rectify a specific religious violation.
key_terms.مَكَانَ كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ: For each time, indicating that each instance of the act requires a separate ruling or expiation.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man pronounces zihar multiple times against his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the jurisprudential principle that each pronouncement of zihar constitutes a distinct act requiring its own expiation, rather than a single cumulative penalty. This ruling is derived from the specific phrasing in Surah Al-Mujadila, emphasizing the individual accountability for each verbal act of separation. It highlights the Shia scholarly focus on precise linguistic interpretation of legal terms within the Quranic text.
